{{Top}}
{{Quote|You've been working in the same sectors too long, Jack...makes for comfortable pirating but narrows your view of the universe.|[[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]]|<ref name="Star Wars (1977) 11">[[Star Wars (1977) 11|''Star Wars'' (1977) 11]]</ref>}}
[[File:Tapani.jpg|thumb|right|200px|The [[Tapani sector/Legends|Tapani sector]], in the [[Colonies/Legends|Colonies]] region of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]]]
A '''sector''' was an area of [[Realspace/Legends|space]] framed by an artificial boundary for [[Politics/Legends|political]], economic and military organization.

==History==
Groupings of inhabited systems organized themselves into informal sectors from before the [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]]. The [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] was the first body to attempt a large scale application of standardized sectors. A sector was defined by the Republic as having a maximum of 50 inhabited [[Star system/Legends|star systems]] to keep sectors at a manageable level.<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref>

The rapid exploration, expansion and colonization beginning around [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]] caused many sectors to grow larger than the intended size. For instance, in [[19 ABY/Legends|19 ABY]], the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Remnant]] controlled only eight sectors, which were said to contain "over a thousand inhabited systems,"<ref name="Specter of the Past">''[[Specter of the Past]]''</ref> which would indicate an average size of 125 inhabited systems per sector. At some point in the history of the galaxy, there were millions of sectors, as populations grew rapidly. The [[Ruusan Reformations/Legends|Ruusan Reformation]] of [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]] reorganized the galaxy into 1,024 regional sectors, which were divided into even smaller constituent subsectors.<ref name="TEA" />

[[File:Galaxymap3.jpg|thumb|left|260px|Map of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], including [[Planet/Legends|planets]] and sectors]]
The Ruusan Reformations were problematic, however, as they created a moratorium on the creation of new sectors; meanwhile, beings continued to inhabit worlds beyond the borders of the established Republic. This led to annexation and overinflation of existing sectors. For example, the lightly populated [[Chommell sector/Legends|Chommell sector]] encompassed 36 full-member worlds, more than 40,000 settled dependencies and 300,000,000 barren stars in the final years of the Republic.<ref name="AOTCICS">''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones Incredible Cross-Sections]]''</ref> [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] reversed the moratorium on new regional sectors and created new sectors by dividing up larger ones. Any freestanding subsectors were grouped up into a single sector.<ref name="TEA" />

By Republic law, in state of emergency, an appointed governor-general coordinated military actions with the [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] of a troubled sector. This law was invoked many times during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] by Chancellor Palpatine.<ref name="TEA" />

When the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] took control of the Republic's sectors, [[Moff/Legends|Moffs]] replaced senators as sectorial governors. Sectors were also commonly expanded and collapsed together to consolidate power in the officers Palpatine delegated to rule. Any unincorporated territories wishing for inclusion in the Empire became new freestanding subsectors, and were added to new or existing regional sectors as events warranted.<ref name="TEA" />

Many sectors owed their name to their primary system, which in turn was named after its primary [[Planet/Legends|planet]]. For example the planet [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] belonged to the [[Alderaan system/Legends|Alderaan system]] and thus, to the [[Alderaan sector/Legends|Alderaan sector]].

The word "sector" also denoted subdivisions of planets, especially for [[Ecumenopolis/Legends|ecumenopolis]] such as [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] or [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]], but even on less populated worlds such as [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].
